confirmed.title: report_civic duplicate check is not serialized: two simultaneous reports of the same problem create two tickets
confirmed.trigger: Two phones call rpc('report_civic', { p_kind:'garbage', p_lat, p_lng within 60 m of each other }) at the same moment (e.g. a stage demo of 'ten citizens, one ticket'). Under READ COMMITTED both `select * into existing ...` run before either insert commits.
confirmed.effect: No error. Both calls see no open ticket, both insert: two CIV- serials with signatures = 1 each instead of one ticket with signatures = 2. Later reports attach only to whichever is nearest, so the collective weight stays split.
confirmed.fix:
Optional. In report_civic, replace the single line

  select * into existing from civic_tickets t

with

  -- Serialize reports of the same kind so two simultaneous reports cannot both miss the open ticket.
  perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('report_civic:' || p_kind));

  select * into existing from civic_tickets t
confirmed.why:
The race is real, but it is cosmetic. It cannot make migration 0004 fail and it never raises an error at run time. The fix is optional hardening and should not be a reason for another edit-and-rerun cycle on its own.

**Why the race exists** (`C:\dk\supabase\migrations\0004_media_trust_civic.sql`, lines 87-114)
- `report_civic` is a check-then-insert: it selects the nearest open ticket of the same kind within 60 m, and inserts a new one if none is found.
- Nothing in the schema backs this up. `civic_tickets` has only the primary key, a unique `serial` and a gist index on `geog`; there is no unique or exclusion constraint on kind plus location.
- PostgREST runs each rpc in its own READ COMMIT
